title: Grouping & Ordering
description: Stack overlapping shapes in order, group them so they move as one, and ungroup them again.

bubble.title: Groups and stacking order
bubble.body: Where shapes overlap, one is in front. Grouping ties shapes together so they move, scale, and copy as one object. Both are decisions about the selection.

bubble.title: Draw two shapes
bubble.body: Steer to a corner and press I to start the first of two overlapping shapes.

bubble.title: First shape down
bubble.body: Steer to the opposite corner and press I again to deposit it.

bubble.title: Second shape
bubble.body: Press I again to start a second shape, overlapping the first.

bubble.title: Second shape down
bubble.body: Steer and press I again. Where they overlap, the newer shape sits in front.

bubble.title: Restack them
bubble.body: The second shape is still selected, and it sits in front where they overlap. Choose Object ▸ Order ▸ Send to Back — it drops behind the first shape. Order lives in the Object menu and the Arrange section.

bubble.title: Select both
bubble.body: Click the first shape, then Shift+click the second, so both are selected. Grouping needs at least two.

bubble.title: Group them
bubble.body: Choose Object ▸ Group ▸ Group (Ctrl/Cmd+G). The two shapes become one object: select it, drag it, and they travel together.

bubble.title: Ungroup them
bubble.body: Choose Object ▸ Group ▸ Ungroup. The group dissolves back into its two shapes — grouping is a wrapper, never a merge. (Merging shapes for real is Combinatorics.)

bubble.title: The list view of all this
bubble.body: The Layers & Objects section lists every object in stacking order — the same front-to-back story, as a list you can click, hide, and reorder.
